correctness.rationale: The oriented incidence matrix of a connected cactus has rank |V|-1. Its independent balanced even-cycle relations account for its entire affine kernel and yield an affine join of cycle factors plus bridge singletons. Each even cycle factor is a free sum of two equal-dimensional simplices and has uniquely centered asymmetry half its length minus one. The explicit affine-join reflection argument gives exact global lower bound and forces every factor center and join weight, proving uniqueness. Distinct-edge reflection identities give the matching upper bound. 270 exact-rational cacti and 3685 reflection equations were replayed from included verify.py, corroborating rather than replacing proof.

value.rationale: This gives a complete closed asymmetry invariant, unique center, exact edge-specific reflection certificates, and an orientation-independent structural law for all connected semi-balanced cactus graphs. Arbitrary numbers and arrangements of cycles/bridges are covered. The bridge versus cycle coefficient separation is exact and cannot be guessed by graph size alone. The question relates natural graph-root geometry to a classical affine invariant; it is not a finite table or trivial sign normalization.
